P01.passage: About nine thousand years ago, a tongue of lava poured into a narrow mountain valley and hardened across the floor where a river had wound in wide loops. The flow sealed the valley from wall to wall, with no low saddle for the water to escape over, and the river, rising behind it, became a lake without an outlet; the lake loses water only to evaporation, since the lava under it is solid rock with no cracks. Mapping the valley today, geologists conclude that the lava ______ the river.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: In 2015 a small software firm began working with independent restaurants in one mid-sized city. Restaurants paid it to appear in its weekly videos, and lines formed outside each one the morning after it was featured, an approach local newspapers had used for decades. Diners still dealt with restaurants directly, and the firm took no part when a diner and a restaurant disagreed about a bill. By 2018, most of the city's restaurant owners spoke of the firm as their trade's ______.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigning for a shorter working day began publishing a weekly newspaper. Throughout the campaign it printed only meeting notices, took no side on policy, and won few readers beyond the members, yet the branches relied on its press and its funds for everything, never building any of their own; when the paper closed, the movement fell apart within months. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum beside the painter's other early work. The painter made it in the year his teacher died, recreating the teacher's best-known harbor scene in the teacher's own manner and signing it with both of their names; he never offered it for sale, and it changed nothing about how he painted afterward. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: In the 1930s, two small research teams lowered thermometers into holes drilled in the seabed to measure how much heat escapes from the ocean floor. Their values were accurate, and later surveys of the ocean floor found nearly the same numbers, but they appeared while geologists were absorbed in other debates, went uncited for forty years, and played no part in how the field's ideas developed; no later survey was calibrated against them. Historians of geology now regard those two measurements as ______ in the history of their field.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It granted each tenant family a permanent right to stay and each landowner a permanent right to the old rents, so neither side could ever yield; the quarrels went on at once in the same village courts as before, never growing more bitter, but passing unsettled from parents to children for three generations. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf. She first used gold in 1960 and planned it in careful sketches, spreading it across most of each background, but only in portraits of the bankers who had once refused her loans, whom she painted as small, pinched figures nearly swallowed by the glittering wealth they prized. One critic who has examined those late canvases closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: Every spring a colony of flightless ground beetles nests on a gravel bar in the middle of a western river, feeding on the seeds of low plants that grow there. The water never reached the nests, and the gravel spit joining the bar to the bank stayed above it, but the flood drowned the ants that live on the low riverbank and raid the nests for larvae each summer; with the ants gone, the colony raised twice its usual number of young. After surveying the bar in July, one ecologist reported that the year's flood had ______ the colony.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: For centuries a dry foothill ridge has been covered by pines, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a drought lasting seven years struck the ridge. Almost every pine survived, and the oaks stayed as scattered as before, but the pines' growth slowed sharply during the drought and never recovered: trees that were saplings then are still barely half the height of pines the same age on wetter slopes, and they suffered as badly as ever in the next dry spell. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. Instead of buying a commercial catalog from a large vendor in 2018, technicians kept the old program running under its old name, fixing each flaw as borrowers reported it with a few lines of new code. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy about a queen torn between duty and love. The company kept every scene and performed each with grave sincerity, adding nothing, but it shuffled their order, opening with the queen's death and closing with her first meeting with the young soldier, so that audiences who did not know the text struggled to follow the story. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: Last spring, the council of one river town replaced the property tax that paid for trash pickup with a monthly fee charged to each household. Bills began with the next month's pickup, larger, costlier homes paid more than small ones, and an audit confirmed the fee just covered the cost of hauling. But each bill showed only a single number, and residents who asked how theirs had been calculated were told the formula was confidential. Several council members objected that the fee, as written, was ______.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: In 2019 an orbiting telescope that tracks the brightness of thousands of stars recorded a drop in the light of one star that had shone steadily for years. The star's light fell by half over two full years and then climbed back over two full years, each month of the recovery retracing a month of the decline in reverse, sliding smoothly from start to finish without a pause along the way. After studying the telescope's record of the event, one astronomer described the dimming as ______.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. The glacier has lost a great deal of ice, plainly visible in the crews' photographs, and has never regained any of it, but nearly all of the loss came in three summers, 1962, 1988, and 2011, when parts of the front collapsed; in the years between, the measurements barely moved. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Students from the two towns had long played an informal game each autumn under rules older than anyone could remember; the school began charging admission to it, and shopkeepers in both towns sold rival pennants, while posters told the bridge quarrel just as the court papers did and the crowds grew rowdier each year. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had already begun writing in that style, and its editor printed whatever they brought him without changing a line; he let them hold their meetings and readings in the room above the shop, and the group, which met nowhere else, grew quickly there. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Its members kept their workshops in every quarter of the city and kept making glassware, but a shared furnace design let each shop fire twice as many pieces a week; glass grew so cheap and common that the city's nobles stopped giving it as gifts. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: A sociologist spent three years observing the Saturday market of a small farming town. Its stalls sold the same goods every week, but the town's two church congregations fought there each Saturday over which faction would get the best stalls, shouting down any speaker from the other side, and the quarrels often ended in fistfights that the police had to break up. By the 1950s, the sociologist concluded, the market mattered to the town less for its trade than as its principal ______.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: Each autumn, several thousand snow geese leave their nesting grounds on the northern tundra and fly some three thousand kilometers south to coastal marshes. That year the flocks, no larger than usual, left together in the usual week, but storms had already frozen the southern half of the route, so they flew no farther than a chain of ice-free lakes halfway down and spent the whole winter there before turning north in spring. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. No charter, lord, or court granted its powers, and it had no guards or fines; the five eldest heads of household decided every question, and villagers obeyed them because such councils had settled grazing "as our grandfathers did" for as long as anyone remembered. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 exactly as written and in the order they had been found, adding no pictures, but after nearly every stanza she inserted a paragraph of her own recalling where her aunt had been when she wrote it, so that few poems can be read straight through. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: In 1893, during a deep economic slump, a mid-sized industrial city began giving aid to families out of work. Its clerk designed the program alone, ignoring the charity methods then popular elsewhere, and it ran unchanged for thirty years; a family applied on a single short form and received only enough flour and coal for a week, while the city spent a tenth of what neighboring cities did per family. In her history of the city, one scholar described its relief program of the 1890s as above all ______.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. Its code was freely shared, and it was the most advanced system of its day; it was assembled from separate parts that could each be swapped out on its own, though a fault in any one part still crashed the whole machine. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: Farmers in one northern valley once built hundreds of dry stone walls, and today the walls are coated with lichens, slow-growing crusts of fungus and algae. The crusts spread onto the walls from nearby cliffs after the walls were built, and they grow at no steady rate and shrug off polluted air, but as they slowly break down the surface of the rock they trap blown dust into a thin soil, in which mosses and then ferns take root. In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: Starting in 2019, the tenants of a large apartment complex spent two years in talks with its owner over rents and repairs. They had already formed their own committee, whose young chair did all the bargaining; before each session the association's director met privately with her, coaching her on what to ask for and when to hold firm, then stayed away from the talks themselves. Looking back, many residents described the neighborhood association as the tenants' ______.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: Facing a budget gap in 2021, one rural school district reviewed the twelve bus routes that carried its students to class. It kept running all twelve routes itself, but each now followed different streets, laid out so that no child walked more than a quarter mile to a stop, and the savings came entirely from buses burning less fuel on shorter loops. By the following autumn, the district had ______ its bus routes.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The charge matched the figure on the school's flyer to the cent and was paid once, with nothing returned at graduation, but at fourteen hundred dollars it was more than most families in the district could pay, and half the students went without. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: In 1974, one small coastal state set a minimum price that dealers had to pay its fishers for lobster. Lobster prices had held steady for years, so the floor rarely mattered; courts upheld it, and lawmakers quietly repealed it in 1980. Yet when the state later set minimum prices for clams and scallops, legislators cited the lobster rule as proof that such a law could survive in court. Historians of the fishery now regard the price floor as the state's clearest ______.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: At nineteen, a poet mailed a sheaf of her poems to a novelist she admired, and he answered with a long letter of advice and judgment. Through the hungry years when no editor would answer her, she reread its closing promise that she would one day be widely read whenever she thought of quitting, and that promise kept her at her desk, though she thought his specific advice was wrong and later gave the letter itself away to a library. Long after the novelist's death, the letter remained the poet's ______.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright added it during rehearsals to cover a change of scenery: it halts the quarrel for a wordless dance by the servants, after which brother and sister stand exactly where they stood before, and audiences have always loved it. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: In 1958 a jazz singer published a memoir of her forty years onstage, years that included a divorce, a bankruptcy, and a long feud with the band she had founded. She gives whole chapters to the divorce and the bankruptcy, recording the unheated rooms, the pawned dresses, and the nights she slept in bus stations, and she is as unsparing toward her former bandmates as toward herself, in prose she had revised for a decade. Reviewing the book in a literary weekly, one critic called it ______.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. Its envoys spent four years on it, refusing a quick truce, and its three hundred clauses set fees for every cargo and settled cases as rare as a ship blown into the wrong port, though all in polite formulas that never named the seizures that had prompted the talks; joint courts enforced it for a century. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
